# `canair memory`

```
usage: canair memory [-h] <kind> ...

Read ECU memory with ReadMemoryByAddress (0x23) into dumps kept on this machine, and list, compare and export them. Choose a kind:
  dump    read address ranges into a new dump (talks to the car)
  ls      list the dumps
  show    summarise a dump, or hex-dump a range of it
  diff    the runs of addresses that differ between two dumps
  export  write a dump as Intel HEX, S-record or binary
  set     set an ECU's memory format, largest block or session

Find which ranges an ECU answers with `canair scan memory`.

positional arguments:
  <kind>
    dump      Read address ranges into a local dump
    ls        List the dumps (offline)
    show      Summarise a dump, or hex-dump a range of it
    diff      The address runs whose bytes differ between two dumps of one ECU
    export    Write a dump as Intel HEX, S-record or raw binary
    set       Set an ECU's memory format, largest block or session (writes
              ecus/)

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit

the loop that finds a RAM variable:
  canair scan memory BCM --range FEDE0000-FEDFFFFF
  canair memory dump BCM FEDE0000-FEDFFFFF --label "lights off"
  canair memory dump BCM FEDE0000-FEDFFFFF --label "lights on"
  canair memory diff BCM/20261105-2210-lights-off BCM/20261105-2212-lights-on
  canair pids upsert-param BCM 23/FEDE1234+02 LIGHT_STATE B04

Dumps can hold OEM software and secrets: they stay in your config directory and nothing
that shares a profile can reach them.
```

## `canair memory dump`

```
usage: canair memory dump [-h] [--block N] [--label TEXT] [--format ALFID|kwp]
                          [--session] [--mode HEX] [--throttle-ms THROTTLE_MS]
                          [--yes] [--wican WICAN]
                          [--transport {slcan-tcp,wican-ws,elm327-tcp}]
                          [--no-fallback] [--wait] [--elm-timeout MS]
                          [--timeout SECONDS] [--no-learn-frames] [--json]
                          [--verbose] [--timings] [--reboot] [--unsafe]
                          [--force]
                          ECU START-END[,…]

Read address ranges of one ECU into a new dump. The block size alternates
between N and N-1 bytes so a reply to the previous request is always caught by
its length; a block that does not come back whole is halved. A refused range
is recorded as a gap with its NRC, and a locked one (securityAccessDenied) is
left alone. A keypress (s or escape) or Ctrl-C stops the dump and keeps what
was read. Asks before the first read (--yes to skip).

positional arguments:
  ECU                   ECU name or TX id
  START-END[,…]         Hex address ranges

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --block N             Bytes per read (default: the ECU's memory.max_block,
                        else 64)
  --label TEXT          A label for the dump
  --format ALFID|kwp    Memory format when the ECU declares none: a UDS ALFID
                        (24 = 2-byte size, 4-byte address) or kwp. Saved by
                        `canair memory set` or `canair scan memory`.
  --session             Open a diagnostic session first (--mode, else the
                        ECU's memory.session, else 03)
  --mode HEX            Session mode for --session
  --throttle-ms THROTTLE_MS
                        Delay in ms between reads (default 20)
  --yes, -y             Skip the confirmation before the first read
  --wican WICAN         WiCAN address: ap or IP (default: config
                        transport.host / default_wican=ap)
  --transport {slcan-tcp,wican-ws,elm327-tcp}
                        CAN transport: slcan-tcp (raw CAN), wican-ws (WiCAN
                        ELM327 WebSocket), or elm327-tcp (direct ELM327
                        adapter over TCP). Overrides the config
                        `transport.type` (default: slcan-tcp).
  --no-fallback         Don't auto-fall-back to other configured devices when
                        the selected one is unreachable (see config
                        transport.fallback).
  --wait                Keep retrying to reach the device indefinitely, then
                        start as soon as it comes online (Ctrl-C to stop). For
                        'monitor', also reconnects forever if the connection
                        drops mid-session (auto-failover to another same-
                        transport device is bounded by default; --wait makes
                        it unbounded).
  --elm-timeout MS      ELM327 ECU response timeout in ms (sent as ATSTxx
                        after init)
  --timeout SECONDS     Overall UDS response timeout in seconds (default 3.0
                        ELM / 2.0 raw). Overrides any per-ECU
                        response_timeout_ms for the whole run.
  --no-learn-frames     Don't write response_frames back into the profile's
                        ecus/ when this session confirms how many CAN frames a
                        PID's response occupies (the count that lets the
                        adapter answer without waiting out its full ECU
                        timeout). Use when reading a car the active profile
                        doesn't describe.
  --json                Output results as JSON
  --verbose, -v         Show raw transport traffic and expressions
  --timings             Print per-ECU/PID round-trip timing stats on exit (to
                        stderr)
  --reboot              Reboot WiCAN after session to restore AutoPID mode
                        (skipped on firmware v6, which resumes AutoPID by
                        itself)
  --unsafe              Bypass dangerous command blocklist (requires explicit
                        per-command consent)
  --force               Ask a session already holding the connection to
                        release it, then wait for it
```

## `canair memory ls`

```
usage: canair memory ls [-h] [--json] [ECU]

positional arguments:
  ECU         Only this ECU's dumps

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
  --json      Output as JSON
```

## `canair memory show`

```
usage: canair memory show [-h] [--range START-END] [--json] DUMP

positional arguments:
  DUMP               A dump id (from `memory ls`), prefix or path

options:
  -h, --help         show this help message and exit
  --range START-END  Hex-dump this
  --json             Output as JSON
```

## `canair memory diff`

```
usage: canair memory diff [-h] [--min-run MIN_RUN] [--json] DUMP_A DUMP_B

Compare two dumps of one ECU and list the runs of addresses whose bytes
differ, with both values. Dumps of two software builds are refused: a reflash
moves what an address holds.

positional arguments:
  DUMP_A
  DUMP_B

options:
  -h, --help         show this help message and exit
  --min-run MIN_RUN  Only runs of at least N changed bytes
  --json             Output as JSON
```

## `canair memory export`

```
usage: canair memory export [-h] [--format {ihex,srec,bin}] [--fill HEX]
                            [-o FILE]
                            DUMP

Write a dump for other tools. Intel HEX and S-record keep its holes; a raw
binary needs --fill for one. The file holds ECU memory: keep it local.

positional arguments:
  DUMP

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --format {ihex,srec,bin}
  --fill HEX            bin: the byte to write into holes
  -o, --output FILE     Output file (default stdout)
```

## `canair memory set`

```
usage: canair memory set [-h] [--format ALFID|kwp] [--max-block N]
                         [--session HEX] [--clear {format,max_block,session}]
                         [--dir DIR] [--no-validate]
                         ECU

Set the memory: section of an ECU: the format its reads take, the largest
block that comes back whole and the session they need. `canair scan memory`
writes the same fields from what it finds.

positional arguments:
  ECU

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --format ALFID|kwp    UDS ALFID (e.g. 24) or kwp
  --max-block N         Largest read in bytes
  --session HEX         Session mode the reads need ("03")
  --clear {format,max_block,session}
                        Drop a field (repeatable)
  --dir DIR             ecus/ directory (default: active profile)
  --no-validate         Skip the post-edit schema validation gate
```
